exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Exponential Function, Plus a Constant

question.explanation:
The derivative of $e^{x}$ is just $e^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $-11$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

Using the addition rule, then, we have \begin{eqnarray} \eqalign{ f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(9e^{x} - 11\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(9e^{x}\right) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(-11\right)\\[5pt] & = 9\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} (e^{x}) + 0\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{9e^{x}}. } \end{eqnarray}

question.text: Given that $f(x)=4e^{x} + 17$, the slope of the tangent line at $x=\ln{3}$ is
question.explanation:
The derivative of $e^{x}$ is just $e^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $17$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

First, using the addition rule, we get

\begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 4e^{x} + 17\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(4e^{x}\right) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(17)\\[5pt] & = 4\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(e^{x}\right)+0\\[5pt] & = 4e^{x}. \end{align}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=\ln{3}$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=\ln{3}} &=\left.\left(4e^{x}\right)\,\right|_{x=\ln{3}}\\[3pt] &=4e^{\ln{3}}\\[3pt] &=4\cdot 3\\[3pt] &=\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{12}. } \]

question.text: Given that $f(x)=6x^{7} + 2e^{x}$, the exact value of the slope of the tangent line at $x=-1$ is
question.explanation:
First, using the addition and the power rules, we get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( 6x^{7} + 2e^{x} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( 6x^{7} \right) + \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left( 2e^{x} \right) \\[5pt] & = 6\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(x^{7}\right) + 2\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(e^{x}\right) \\[5pt] & = 6\left(7x^{6}\right) + 2e^{x} \\[5pt] & = 42x^{6} + 2e^{x}. \end{align}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=-1$ is \[ \eqalign{ \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=-1} &=\left.\left( 42x^{6} + 2e^{x} \right)\,\right|_{x=-1}\\[3pt] &= 42(-1)^{6} + 2e^{-1} \\[3pt] &=42\cdot 1 + \dfrac{2}{e}\\[3pt] &=42 + \dfrac{2}{e}. } \]

example.title: Differentiating the Product of a Constant and the Exponential Function, Plus a Polynomial

question.explanation: Using the addition and the power rules, we get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(4e^x-5x^3-4) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(4e^x) - \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(5x^3)-\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(4)\\[5pt] & = 4\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(e^x) - 5\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(x^3)-\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(4)\\[5pt] & = 4e^x - 5(3x^2)-0\\[5pt] & = 4e^x - 15x^2 . \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Base Other Than e

question.explanation:
Applying the formula, we get

\begin{align*} f'(x)&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(6^x-5x^2+6x-19\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(6^x\right)-\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(5x^2\right)+\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(6x\right)-\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(19 \right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(6^x\right)-5\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(x^2\right)+6\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(x\right)-\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(19 \right)\\[5pt] &= \ln 6 \cdot 6^x-5(2x)+6(1)-0\\[5pt] &= 6^{x}\ln 6 -10x+6. \end{align*}

example.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Base Other Than e

question.text: Given that $f(x)=4\cdot 2^x + x^3 - e^2$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$
question.explanation:
Applying the formula, we get \begin{align} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(4\cdot 2^x + x^3 - e^2\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(4\cdot 2^{x} \right)+ \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^3\right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(-e^2 \right) \\[5pt] & = 4\cdot 2^x \ln 2 + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^3\right) + 0 \\[5pt] & = 4\cdot 2^x \ln 2 + 3x^2 . \end{align}

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is \begin{align*} \left.\dfrac {\textrm{d}f} {\textrm{d}x}\right|_{x=0} &= \Big.\left(4\cdot 2^x \ln 2 + 3x^2\right)\Big|_{x=0}\\[3pt] &=4 \cdot 2^{0} \ln 2+ 3\cdot 0^2\\[3pt] &=4\cdot 1\cdot \ln{2} +3\cdot 0\\[3pt] &=4\ln{2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Differentiating an Exponential Function with a Base Other Than e

question.explanation:
Applying the formula, we get

\begin{align*} f'(x)&= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left( 3\cdot 8^{x}+12x+10 \right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left( 3\cdot 8^{x} \right) +\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(12x\right)+\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(10\right)\\[5pt] &= 3\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(8^{x} \right) +12\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(x\right)+\dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}\left(10\right)\\[5pt] &= 3\left(\ln(8) 8^{x}\right) + 12(1) + 0 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{3\ln(8) 8^{x} + 12}. \end{align*}
